claude.rationale: gap_45=1: the deal structurally split the customer-facing physical facility assets (land/improvements) to PropCo/VICI, owned by former creditors and separate from CEC, while the operations that run those facilities stayed on the CEC/OpCo side ("physical assets crossing to former creditors while operations, management and staff stayed on the CEC side") — a documented product/asset-vs-process mismatch across the ownership boundary at closing. This gap was contractually absorbed at closing via three triple-net Lease Agreements, the Management and Lease Support Agreements with CEC guaranty, and the CES Omnibus License and Enterprise Services Agreement, so gap_mitigated=yes. gap_56=0: T5 processes and T6 organization/management/staff both remained together on the CEC side (OpCo continued to operate, executives/employees transitioned to CES serving the members), so operations and the people running them stayed coherently aligned — no T5/T6 split.

gemini.rationale: The transaction split the enterprise into a real-property vehicle (PropCo) and an operating company (OpCo). The physical real-property assets (T4) crossed to PropCo, while the operating processes (T5) and management/staff (T6) remained with OpCo/CEC, creating a structural gap between the physical product/asset and its operations (gap_45=1). This gap was mitigated at closing via long-term triple-net leases and Management and Lease Support Agreements.

openai.rationale: The slice states that only the physical real-property assets crossed to creditor-owned PropCo, while the customer-facing casino and hotel businesses and their operating processes remained with CEC-owned OpCo; therefore no product crossed without its processes, so gap_45 is 0. It also states that operations, management, and staff stayed together on the CEC side, so no process transferred or was re-engineered without its operating organization, making gap_56 0.
